title: Accessing Chern Numbers From Bloch Eigenstates Singularities
authors: Rajesh Asapanna, Rabih El Sokhen, Paolo Aceto, Patrick Popescu-Pampu, Martin Guillot, Jacqueline Bloch, Sylvain Ravets, Clément Hainaut, Alberto Amo, Pierre Delplace
abstract: We propose two methods to extract the Chern numbers of the Bloch bands of a two dimensional insulator, and apply them to a photonic lattice experiment. These two methods require the knowledge of the complex-valued components of the Bloch eigenvectors, or their ratios. Unlike other tomography methods relying on the approximate reconstruction of the Berry curvature and its integration over the Brillouin zone, our methods boil down to the observation of phase vorticities in the eigensates structure. Those measurements, robust to experimental noise, yield exactly quantized values. One of the two methods exploits the non-normalization of the eigenmodes, making it particularly relevant for classical wave systems.
summary: The paper introduces two robust theoretical methods to calculate the Chern number of Bloch bands by analyzing phase singularities directly within the eigenstates, rather than integrating the Berry curvature. These methods are successfully applied to a photonic lattice experiment, confirming that the resulting topological invariant is quantized and independent of gauge choice.
main_problem: The paper proposes novel methods to directly calculate topological invariants, specifically Chern numbers, of Bloch bands by analyzing phase singularities (vorticities) in the eigenstates, bypassing traditional Berry curvature integration.
main_result: Two distinct methods—the 0-section method and the tautological bundle method—were successfully applied to demonstrate that the calculated Chern number is robustly quantized and independent of gauge choice, even when using experimental data from photonic lattices.
method: The core methodology involves identifying zeros (singularities) in continuous sections of complex line bundles formed by Bloch eigenvectors. This leads to calculating topological indices or winding numbers at these zero points across the Brillouin zone torus.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to two-dimensional insulators, demonstrated using a photonic lattice experiment simulating a quantum walk model governed by Floquet operators. The analysis uses concepts from Bloch band theory and complex geometry.
key_observables: Chern number ($C_n$), phase vorticities in eigenstates structure, local indices ($	ext{Ind}_{ ar{k}_j}$), and winding numbers ($W_j[\sigma]$).
important_parameters: The system is characterized by parameters governing the photonic lattice or the Floquet Hamiltonian, leading to topological phases (e.g., $C^+ = -2$ vs. $C^+=0$).
main_assumptions: For the 0-section method, it is crucial that the eigenvector does not vanish on the plaquette when using raw experimental data; for classical wave systems, non-normalization of eigenvectors is exploited.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate reconstructed eigenvectors ($	ilde{\alpha}^+, 	ilde{ eta}^+$) in both topologically trivial ($C=0$) and topological ($C^+=-2$) regimes. They show the relationship between measured data, analytical reconstructions, and the resulting Chern number calculation via index summation.
paper_structure: The paper develops two theoretical methods (0-section and tautological bundle) for calculating $C_n$ from eigenstate zeros. It then applies these methods to a photonic lattice model derived from Floquet theory, demonstrating gauge invariance by comparing results across different gauges and calculation techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimentally accessible route to topological invariants in condensed matter systems using only measurements of wavefunction phases/zeros, which is highly relevant for quantum optics and photonics research.
